Rescuers were on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods Wednesday. Nepal's army was deployed to help rescue more than 100 people believed trapped inside a tunnel at a hydropower plant located in the country's worst-hit district. items.title: Samastha says young women among unrelated men at public events ‘not permissible’
items.summary: A circular issued by the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama led by Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliar has said it is “not permissible” for young women to be present among unrelated men at public roads and stages. The circular has drawn criticism for its outrageous and deeply anti-women language. The circular, issued by Samastha president E Sulaiman Musliar and general secretary Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliar, calls on mahal committees, mosques, madrasas and other institutions to remain vigilant and ensure that Islamic celebrations do not cross what the organisation describes as religious limits. The statement says, “Displaying young women among unrelated men on public roads and stages is not appropriate for believers and is not permissible.” The directive effectively seeks to regulate women’s presence at public religious programmes, placing the onus on local religious leadership to monitor celebrations and ensure that women do not participate alongside unrelated men. The circular comes amid the growing popularity of Milad-e-Sharif celebrations outside traditional religious spaces. items.title: What to do with the words internet gives you: Looming questions after Anupama’s intv
items.summary: Actor Anupama Parameswaran recently spoke about recognising her own relationship in someone else’s words. She didn’t identify the person she was referring to, and there is no need to speculate about their identity. items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A group of 28 pilgrims, including eight members of a family from Visakhapatnam, had a narrow escape during the flash floods in Nepal after their journey was delayed by several hours. The pilgrims, including Visakhapatnam District Level Development Authority (DLDA) chairman Gadu Venkatappa, had travelled from Bhagalpur Airport on August 24 through a private travel operator for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra. According to Venkatappa's brother Garudappal Naidu, the group reached Kathmandu but remained there for three days due to delays in obtaining visas. After receiving the necessary documents, they resumed their journey towards Manasarovar. Speaking to the media, Garudappal said that the group stopped on the way to use a restroom and have tea, which delayed them briefly. Soon after, when their vehicle was about 50-100 metres from a bridge near the China border, a landslide struck the area.
